text:
maria_support: Customer reports intermittent TLS failures since the cert rollover last night in their VPC. They see ~80% success from our control plane checks but app pods inside their private network show handshake errors. They pasted haproxy logs and a short tcpdump.

ryan_network: Any hint of split-horizon DNS or resolver caching on their side?

sre-lina: +1. Our rotator swapped the cert chain and updated VIPs. If their internal resolver still points at the old VIP it could hit a backend with mismatched chain.

maria_support: They ran `dig internal.myapp.internal +short` on a jump host and got 10.4.5.6 (old VIP). Public DNS resolves to 10.4.8.9 (new VIP). TTL was 86400.

engineer-thao: That TTL is the culprit then — long TTL + immediate rollover. Also check whether their sidecars have pinned intermediate fingerprint; we saw a few customers pin exact intermediate before.

maria_support: They confirmed sidecars use a pinned truststore entry (SHA256=AB:CD:...). Their envoy logs show: `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate`.

ryan_network: Two parallel issues: (1) split-horizon/internal resolver cached old VIP -> traffic sent to nodes that still present legacy cert; (2) client-side pining fails when the chain order or intermediate changed.

maria_support: Repro steps I asked them to run: 
- `dig @<their-resolver> internal.myapp.internal +noall +answer` to confirm which IP their resolver returns
- `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` (or restart dnsmasq) on their resolver
- `curl -v --resolve internal.myapp.internal:443:10.4.8.9 https://internal.myapp.internal/` to test against the new VIP
- `systemctl restart envoy` on a sample app node to force truststore reload

engineer-thao: Also asked them to run: `openssl x509 -in /etc/truststore/ca.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256` and paste the fingerprint so we can confirm whether they pinned the intermediate we rotated.

infra-bot: Deploy note: rotator job at 2026-03-15T03:12Z replaced cert chain for cert-id `abc123` with a cross-signed intermediate (order: cross-signed -> root). Previously order was (intermediate -> cross-signed -> root).

maria_support: After flushing DNS and restarting a couple of sidecars they still report ~20% errors. They attached a tcpdump: ClientHello -> SYN to 10.4.5.6 then Server Certificate (new chain) -> client sends Alert and closes.

sre-lina: If the client is still sending SNI for internal.myapp.internal but hits a backend configured with legacy hostname/legacy cert the cert SAN mismatch or a pinned intermediate will cause verification to fail.

ryan_network: Short-term mitigation: ask them to lower internal resolver TTLs and flush caches. Also we can add a compatibility alias route that keeps legacy cert chain available on old VIPs for a limited window.

ops-east: Ops can issue a compat cert bundle keeping the previous intermediate order and push it to the affected AZs. ETA ~1 hour if approved.

engineer-thao: If we provide a compat bundle, they should still restart their sidecars to pick up the resolved chain. Also recommend they remove strict intermediate pining or pin the root instead to avoid this during future cross-sign rotations.

maria_support: I'll update the customer with steps: flush resolver cache, restart proxies, run the `openssl` fingerprint checks, and we can push a compat bundle if they can't roll their pins quickly. Logging this in ticket #12345 and will attach our haproxy log snippets.

ops-east: Proceeding to prepare compat bundle and a limited routing rule to keep both cert variants live for 48h.

maria_support: Thanks — I'll confirm with the customer and request the `dig` output + `openssl` fingerprint. Will follow up here once they confirm. :thumbsup:
